paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how the number of observations (“Counts”) varies across sentiment “Polarity scores,” shown as a single connected line. The x-axis is labeled “Polarity scores,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from about −1.1 on the left to about 0.55 on the right, with labeled ticks appearing at regular 0.2 intervals (−1.0, −0.8, −0.6, −0.4, −0.2, 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6). The y-axis is labeled “Counts,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0 up to just under about 10,000, with labeled ticks at regular 2,000-count intervals (0, 2000, 4000, 6000, 8000). A single blue solid line with circular markers traces the counts at discrete polarity values: counts are near 0 across the most negative scores (around −1.1 to −0.7), rise to roughly ~150 at about −0.6, increase to about ~650 around −0.5 and remain near that level at the next point (around −0.45), dip to about ~350 near −0.4, then climb through approximately ~800 (around −0.3), ~1900 (around −0.2), and ~3100 (around −0.1) before reaching the highest point at 0.0 (approximately ~9200). After the peak, the line drops to about ~3100 at around 0.1, rises again to about ~5100 at around 0.2, declines to about ~2300 at around 0.3, falls near ~0 around ~0.38–0.4, increases to about ~1800 near ~0.45, and then returns close to ~0 at the rightmost point near ~0.55.
